subject: Acme: SLO/SLA language & measurement follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Johnson <alice.johnson@acme.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Acme: post-demo recap + SLO follow-ups

Hi Alice / Ben —

Thanks again for taking the demo this morning. Quick recap and agreed next steps on performance/SLO items we discussed: 

- Target p95 latency: 200ms for single-turn text generation (50-token prompt, 128-token response)
- Target throughput: 500 requests/sec sustained for peak traffic pattern (as discussed)
- Concurrency: initial deployment planned for 200 concurrent sessions, with burst to 400
- Streaming: support required for partial tokens streaming to client SDKs (WebSocket & server-sent events)

Action items we captured: 
1) Acme to confirm whether p95 latency measured from client-side (post-edge) or server-side (Redwood ingress) — Alice to confirm.
2) Redwood (Dev) to provide a brief note on how we measure latency (latency calculation, clock sync assumptions, excluded windows).
3) Redwood legal (Rishi) to propose SLA language covering measurement, reporting cadence, and remedies.
4) Exchange draft SLA and performance appendix — I attached the draft SLA + a spreadsheet template for your perf numbers.

Attachments: draft_sla_redwood_acme_v1.pdf, acme_performance_requirements.xlsx

Next: If we can get the clarification on measurement scope by EOD Wednesday, Rishi will send a proposed SLA redline by Friday and Dev will share measurement details and monitoring endpoints.

Thanks —
Marissa
Sr. Account Executive

From: Alice Johnson <alice.johnson@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2026 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Acme: post-demo recap + SLO follow-ups

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. Quick answers from our side: 

- We generally validate latency from client-side (user-facing) measurements — that’s what our product team cares about. However, we understand network variability, so we can accept server-side measurements if the SLA clearly states the point of measurement plus an agreed network allowance.
- Streaming: yes, we need token-level streaming for the chat UI; important that partial tokens arrive within 150ms once generation starts.
- Throughput: the 500 rps sustained is correct for our early beta; we may need to increase to 800 rps for holiday load.

We’ll review the draft SLA and get back with redlines. Attaching a quick note with our internal expectation mapping (will upload to the Drive link).

Thanks,
Alice
Product Manager, Acme Corp
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Johnson <alice.johnson@acme.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2026 14:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Acme: post-demo recap + SLO follow-ups

Thanks — adding technical details on measurement and exclusions so Rishi can fold them into the SLA appendix. See notes below.

How we measure latency (server-side canonical):
- Measurement point: time between request arrival at Redwood ingress (TLS termination) and final token emitted to Redwood egress (we record last-token send completion).
- Percentile calculation: requests aggregated per 5-minute window; p95 computed over rolling 30-day window for reporting purposes, and p95 over the month for SLA evaluation period unless otherwise agreed.
- Clock sync: ingress and egress timestamps are based on NTP-synced hosts; we include +/- 5ms clock skew tolerance in observability docs.

Exclusions and caveats we typically include:
- Scheduled maintenance windows (with prior notice)
- Outages caused by customer-side network (we detect via edge RTT and include measurement flags)
- Third-party model provider outages for models not fully hosted by Redwood (we’d provide fallbacks/notifications)
- Misconfigured client headers that circumvent streaming (we’ll provide SDK config checks)

Streaming-specific:
- ‘Time to first chunk’ measured from ingress to first byte of streaming chunk; goal = p95 <= 150ms (aligned with your request).
- Partial-token cadence: SDK-level buffer threshold set to 20ms; we guarantee delivery of chunks as generated subject to network conditions.

Monitoring/reporting endpoints: 
- We can provide a read-only metrics endpoint (Prometheus scrape + Grafana dashboards) and a daily SLA report PDF.
- Reporting cadence: automated weekly performance digest; monthly formal SLA report for governance.

I can drop a short appendix (1 page) summarizing this in the draft SLA. Marissa — do you want that attached to Rishi’s redline or sent separately?

—Dev
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Johnson <alice.johnson@acme.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 6 Apr 2026 09:11:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Acme: post-demo recap + SLO follow-ups

Hi Alice — 

Thanks for the prompt answers. I’ve attached a first-pass redline to the draft SLA (draft_sla_redwood_acme_v1.pdf) that incorporates Dev’s measurement notes and the exclusions we typically use. Highlights: 

- Measurement point: we propose server-side canonical measurement with an explicit ‘customer-facing allowance’ clause. Language: "Latency is measured at Redwood ingress-to-egress. Customer-facing latency is specifically defined as ingress-to-egress plus an allowance of up to 30ms to account for CDN/edge transit, unless Customer provides alternative agreed measurement methods in writing."
- Reporting cadence: weekly automated digests; monthly formal SLA report with p95/p99 tables and incident timelines.
- Remedies: 1) Service credits starting at 2% of monthly invoice for failure to meet p95 in a billing month (thresholds and caps specified). 2) Escalation path and 72-hour remediation timeline for repeated breaches.
- Exclusions: explicit callouts for scheduled maintenance, force majeure, customer network, and third-party model provider failures.

Open items I’d like Acme to confirm: 
1) Acceptance of server-side canonical measurement + 30ms allowance OR provide an observed client-side measurement stream for direct comparison.
2) Whether the credit scale below (2% baseline, 5% repeated) is acceptable.
3) Exact reporting contact for monthly reports (email + pager if you have SRE on-call).

I’ve kept the language fairly standard but happy to tighten the definitions if you prefer stronger SLAs for p95/p99 or alternate remedies.

Next steps: if you can confirm the three open items, I’ll produce a turn-key DocuSign-ready redline and we can loop procurement.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Legal (Commercial Contracts)
Redwood Inference
From: Alice Johnson <alice.johnson@acme.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 6 Apr 2026 11:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Acme: SLO/SLA language & measurement follow-up

Rishi / team — thanks, that redline looks good as a starting point. Quick responses: 

1) We can accept server-side canonical measurement with the 30ms customer-facing allowance for the initial contract. We will also provide client-side telemetry during the beta to compare.
2) The credit scale is acceptable for now; we’ll reserve the right to revisit for the peak season uplift.
3) Reporting contact: please send monthly SLA reports to infra-reports@acme.com and cc our SRE on-call pager (pager@acme.com) for any incident escalations.

We’ll review the DocuSign when available. Once Rishi locks the redline, we’ll run through procurement and aim to sign before the beta kickoff.

Thanks —
Alice
Product Manager, Acme Corp
